llm_judge_report.task_name: Prepare two hamburgers and a salad

relevance.justification: Messages were highly focused on the task, addressing role allocation, ingredient gathering, and failure reporting, though repetitive failure reports reduced overall necessity.

clarity.justification: Messages were unambiguous, well-structured, and explicitly stated current locations, intentions, and reasons for failure.

grounding.justification: All statements were factually consistent with the simulator state, accurately reporting missing tools (knife), inventory contents, and workstation conflicts.

coordination_utility.justification: Communication failed to resolve the main bottleneck. Despite multiple agents reporting a missing knife, no one coordinated to find it, leading to repeated failures and a stalled task.

redundancy.justification: There was severe repetition regarding the missing knife. Four out of the seven total messages were nearly identical reports of CUT failures due to the missing tool.

planning_coherence.justification: While initial role allocation made sense, agents repeatedly violated task dependencies by attempting to assemble without cut ingredients and attempting to cut without first locating a knife.

failure_explanation_quality.justification: Agents clearly and accurately diagnosed the cause of their failures (e.g., missing knife, workstation conflicts), but failed to propose or execute constructive recovery plans to acquire the missing tool.

llm_judge_report.overall_summary: The team communicated clearly and accurately diagnosed their physical constraints, but suffered from poor coordination utility and high redundancy. They repeatedly reported the same missing tool error without ever replanning to resolve the bottleneck, resulting in task failure.
